Autoimmune peripheral neuropathy confined predominantly to the legs; weakness reflects nerve dysfunction, without primary muscle disease.
COL9A2-related epiphyseal cartilage and joint disease; tooth agenesis occurs in only 1/4 reported patients.

Postinfectious systemic inflammation; cardiac dysfunction affects roughly 50–80%, and intestinal inflammation >30%. Transient rash and conjunctival injection excluded.
Benign papillomas confined to breast ducts; breast has no axis.
MED13-related neurodevelopmental disorder with universal developmental delay; constipation in 4/13 does not establish intrinsic bowel damage; Duane anomaly in 2/13.
Demyelinating sensorimotor neuropathy and defining severe early scoliosis; hearing, ocular and respiratory abnormalities each occur in <30%.
Hereditary susceptibility to neuroblastoma, a sympathetic neural tumour; the defining target axis is neurologic, without assuming existing tumour or additional damage.
Isolated microphthalmia and coloboma define ocular disease; holoprosencephaly and orofacial cleft are occasional, below 30%.
Defining skeletal abnormalities and hearing loss; intellectual disability in 11/12 and global developmental delay in 13/22 support neurologic involvement.
Inherited oocyte/embryo maturation defect causing female infertility; purely reproductive dysfunction without evidence of endocrine gland disease.
Inherited lipoate metabolism defect; neurologic regression, white-matter disease and cerebellar atrophy in reported cases (1/1). Hepatic and cardiovascular frequencies unclear.
Glycosylation defect with encephalopathy and deafness (80–100%); reduced visual acuity 3/3. Arthrogryposis (80–99%) and coagulopathy (30–79%) omitted by cap.
In situ carcinoma of nasopharyngeal airway epithelium; tumour association with EBV does not itself establish an infectious disease.
Familial gastric carcinoma arises in the stomach; associated hereditary syndromes and other cancers do not establish additional organ involvement across this group.
Mature B-cell lymphoma; oral cavity neoplasm is frequent (30–79%), supporting gastrointestinal occupation. Hepatic and pancreatic abnormalities are occasional.
Heterogeneous disorders of histiocyte accumulation; skin, liver, skeletal and neurologic damage vary by subtype, without a reliably shared additional organ.
Inherited cerebral white-matter disease; feeding difficulty and tube feeding do not establish intrinsic gastrointestinal damage.
Isolated vaginal developmental absence, sometimes with uterine agenesis; reproductive tract disease has no axis.
Progressive retinal pigment epithelial dystrophy causing visual loss; associated structural findings are also confined to the eye.
Congenital absence or transverse reduction of limbs defines musculoskeletal malformation; no additional organ disease is documented.
Immune-mediated cutaneous lichen planus with photodistributed lichenoid lesions; no common extracutaneous damage established for this variant.
Autoimmune destruction of gastric body/fundic mucosa; pernicious anaemia is a separate disease, and gastric carcinoma is a later risk.
Defining developmental brain and hand/foot abnormalities; hearing impairment occurs in 30–79%. Unspecified eye abnormalities and facial dysmorphism do not prove ocular damage.
